title.en: Learning frontend development when AI can write the code
title.zh: AI 对前端的冲击很大，我想怎样继续学下去

summary.en: A personal reflection on the pressure of AI coding, the fundamentals I want to keep, and a practical way to learn through small, reviewed changes.
summary.zh: 代码越来越容易生成，前端还要学什么？记录我对这份压力的看法，以及接下来怎样练习用 AI 开发、读懂改动和验证结果。

basis.en: Personal views and a proposed learning routine, connected to the project notes linked below. This is an essay about how I want to learn, rather than a measurement of jobs or productivity.
basis.zh: 结合近期项目笔记，整理个人看法和下一步学习打算。文中的开发流程与任务说明可作为练习参考。

title.en: The pressure feels close to the work
title.zh: 以前熟悉的工作，正在变得更容易生成

paragraphs.en: AI's impact on frontend work feels substantial to me. Producing a first version of a form or page is becoming easier, and that puts pressure on skills built around implementing familiar patterns. It leaves me wondering how much of what I already know will remain useful, and what I should spend time learning next.
paragraphs.zh: 我觉得 AI 对前端的冲击确实很大。一个表单、一套页面，以前需要花时间逐个实现，现在借助 AI 就能先得到一个像样的版本。对于把写页面当作主要能力的开发者，这种变化很难没有压力。我也会想，原来学的东西还够不够，接下来应该把时间花在哪里。

paragraphs.en: I want AI-assisted development to become part of my regular learning. There are details I still need to understand myself: why a component rerenders, where its data comes from, and what happens when a request fails. If I cannot follow the code after it is generated, the next change becomes harder to judge.
paragraphs.zh: 我的想法是，把 AI 辅助开发纳入日常学习，同时保持自己读代码的能力。组件为什么重新渲染、数据从哪里来、请求失败后页面怎么办，这些问题仍然要弄明白。生成完代码却看不懂，下一次需求变化时就很难判断该怎么改。

title.en: The fundamentals give me a way to judge the output
title.zh: 基础知识，决定我能不能看出生成代码的问题

paragraphs.en: The recent request-scope note provides a useful example. A search box can look finished while an older response still overwrites the latest results. After an account switch, a pending response also needs to be checked against its original identity. Recognising these cases requires an understanding of asynchronous execution and state ownership.
paragraphs.zh: 最近整理的请求作用域笔记，就是一个很具体的例子。搜索框看起来已经能用，旧请求却可能覆盖新结果；切换账号后，之前发出的响应也可能继续回来。要看出这类问题，需要理解异步执行和状态归属。只看截图，很容易把功能判断得过早。

paragraphs.en: I want to keep learning JavaScript's event loop, TypeScript data boundaries, browser behaviour and component lifecycles through problems like this. CSS layout, keyboard navigation and HTTP also remain part of that work. These topics help me explain a change and decide whether its behaviour matches the requirement.
paragraphs.zh: 所以 JavaScript 的事件循环、TypeScript 的数据边界、浏览器行为和组件生命周期，我都还要继续学。CSS 布局、键盘操作、HTTP 请求也一样。最好带着实际问题去学：遇到迟到响应，就把相关代码和异步机制一起看；遇到弹窗，就检查焦点和键盘能不能正常使用。

title.en: Give AI a task that can be reviewed
title.zh: 把任务说小一点，把验收说清楚一点

paragraphs.en: A workflow I want to practise starts with a small change. I would give the assistant the relevant files, dependency versions, expected behaviour and known constraints, then ask it to explain the current implementation before editing. A bounded change is easier to inspect in a diff and easier to undo if the approach is wrong.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来我想练习的方式，是先选一个范围清楚的小改动，把相关文件、依赖版本、预期行为和现有限制提供给 AI，再让它说明当前实现。一次改动控制得小一些，自己看 diff 时更容易弄清楚每一处为什么要改，方案不合适时也方便回退。

paragraphs.en: For an asynchronous search exercise, the task brief below makes the expected behaviour explicit. It is a proposed exercise based on the request-scope discussion, and would still need to be adapted to the project's actual API and test commands.
paragraphs.zh: 例如练习修复搜索竞态时，可以用下面这样的任务说明。它需要结合项目实际接口和测试命令调整，重点是把“怎样才算修好”提前说清楚。

bullets.en: Read the search component and its request helper. Explain how results, errors and loading state are currently updated.
bullets.zh: 先阅读搜索组件与请求封装，说明结果、错误提示和加载状态分别在哪里更新。

bullets.en: For rapid searches A then B, only B may update the current results, error or loading state, even if A finishes later. Preserve the existing interface and visual layout.
bullets.zh: 快速依次搜索 A、B 时，只允许 B 更新当前结果、错误提示和加载状态，即使 A 更晚结束。保留现有接口与页面布局。

bullets.en: Cover stale success and stale failure, and check what happens when the page is left. Use the existing test setup and report the commands and their actual output.
bullets.zh: 覆盖旧请求迟到成功、迟到失败，并检查离开页面后的回调。沿用项目测试方式，提供实际运行的命令和输出。

bullets.en: Explain each changed file and any remaining gaps. Keep unrelated cleanup out of this change so the diff stays reviewable.
bullets.zh: 说明每个文件的修改原因和仍未覆盖的情况，让这次 diff 只围绕当前问题展开。

title.en: I need to be able to explain the change
title.zh: AI 写完之后，我要能讲清楚这段代码

paragraphs.en: After a change, I would read the diff and run the checks myself. A useful review asks where data enters, which state can change, and how failure is handled. If I cannot explain an unfamiliar helper, I can ask for a walkthrough and then check the explanation against the code and the relevant documentation.
paragraphs.zh: AI 写完之后，我需要自己读改动、运行检查。数据从哪里进入，哪些状态会改变，失败后怎样处理，至少要能顺着代码讲清楚。遇到不熟悉的函数，可以让 AI 解释，再对照源码和官方文档核实。解释听起来顺畅，并不能代替这个过程。

paragraphs.en: The low-code form notes suggest concrete cases to try: required numeric zero, invalid dates, and duplicate field keys. For an upload component, reaching 100% transfer progress still leaves the question of whether processing is complete. These cases help me connect a feature's appearance to its actual contract.
paragraphs.zh: 低代码表单笔记里提到的零值、无效日期、重复字段标识，都可以拿来做检查。上传组件的进度到了 100%，也还要确认后续处理是否完成。这些问题很细，却直接影响使用体验。我希望能把这类检查习惯带进 AI 辅助开发，而不是每次只确认页面打开了。

paragraphs.en: When asking an assistant to diagnose a problem, I can use a minimal example and synthetic data. The useful context is the interface shape, failure and surrounding code; real account details and private business records do not need to accompany the example.
paragraphs.zh: 向 AI 描述问题时，可以使用最小示例和模拟数据，提供接口结构、报错和相关代码。真实账号信息和业务记录无需跟着示例一起提交。这样也能逼着自己先把问题提炼清楚。

title.en: What I want to practise next
title.zh: 接下来，给自己留一些能做下去的练习

paragraphs.en: For the next round of study, I want to choose one small feature in an existing project, write down the acceptance conditions, work through an AI-assisted change, and leave a short review. The review can record which suggestion was useful, which was rejected, and which part I still cannot explain. That should give the next learning session somewhere specific to start.
paragraphs.zh: 下一轮学习，我想从现有项目中选一个小功能，先写验收条件，再尝试用 AI 完成修改，最后留下一段复盘：哪条建议有用，哪条没有采用，还有哪段代码自己说不清楚。这样下一次学习就有明确的起点，也能看出自己究竟补上了什么。

paragraphs.en: There are already suitable questions in the recent notes: test an old request that fails after a newer request succeeds, reduce the shared layer's broad any types, or observe memory use while hashing a large file. I would keep a brief record of the environment, changes and actual results, including anything that remains unresolved.
paragraphs.zh: 近期笔记中已经有合适的题目：补测新请求成功后旧请求才报错的情况，逐步收紧共享层的 any 类型，或者观察大文件计算哈希时的内存占用。每次记下环境、改动与实际结果，没解决的地方也保留下来。

paragraphs.en: Learning new AI tools matters to me, but I also want time to finish and understand these exercises. My next note should be able to show a specific change, explain why I accepted it, and link to a check that someone else can repeat.
paragraphs.zh: 新的 AI 工具需要了解，已经开始的练习也要留时间做完、弄懂。我希望下一篇笔记能够拿出一个具体改动，解释自己为什么接受它，再附上别人可以复跑的检查。用这样的记录，看看自己有没有真的学会。
